standard_prerequisites.name: Simplicial set, horn and Kan fibration
standard_prerequisites.statement: The Kan condition (every horn extends) and the notion of a trivial Kan fibration, which additionally induces surjections in every degree.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the conclusion and the shape of what has to be verified (source lines 6210, 6213-6220).

standard_prerequisites.name: Skeleton and coskeleton
standard_prerequisites.statement: The n-skeleton and n-coskeleton functors on simplicial sets and the canonical morphisms from an object to the coskeleton of its skeleton.
standard_prerequisites.use: The hypotheses (3) and (4) are the isomorphisms with the coskeleton, used in the high-dimensional case (source lines 6205-6208, 6225-6237).

standard_prerequisites.name: Standard simplex and its boundary
standard_prerequisites.statement: The standard k-simplex with its boundary, and the fact that for k > n the n-skeletons of the two coincide.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what makes the extension automatic for horns of dimension greater than n (source lines 6230-6237).

core_obligations: Set up the horn filling: given a horn in V over a map of its boundary into U, use the hypotheses in low degrees to extend it there (source lines 6213-6220).
Handle horns of dimension at most n: use the bijectivity for degrees below n and the surjectivity in degree n to produce the required extension (source lines 6220-6229).

Handle horns of dimension greater than n: use the coskeletal hypotheses together with the identity of the n-skeleta of the standard simplex and its boundary to obtain a unique dotted arrow, completing the verification that f is a trivial Kan fibration (source lines 6230-6237).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the Kan condition to filling horns and set up the boundary data.
Fill horns of dimension at most n using bijectivity below n and surjectivity at n.
Fill higher horns via the coskeletal hypotheses and the skeleton coincidence.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-section at source lines 6198-6211: for a morphism f : V -> U of simplicial sets, if f is a bijection in degrees below n, a surjection in degree n, and both V and U are isomorphic to the n-coskeleton of their n-skeleta, then f is a trivial Kan fibration. The proof at source lines 6213-6238 is a horn-filling argument that has to be run in two regimes. For a horn of dimension at most n the filling comes from the bijectivity in low degrees together with the surjectivity in degree n; for a horn of dimension greater than n the proof uses the coskeletal hypotheses to show that the relevant skeleton of the standard simplex coincides with that of its boundary, which makes the extension automatic and produces the dotted arrow. Both regimes must be treated and the statement mentions neither the skeleton computations nor the case split. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
